rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly, so the primary adjustment is raising SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights across all seven passes to push selection coverage on this small 7-function, 6.5KB-text program where every function matters. SUB stays dominant: arithmetic substitution is cheap, low-risk, and especially effective here because sphereflake is floating-point-heavy (v_t/vector math, intersect templates), where expression rewiping resists symbolic simplification. SPLIT is kept high with near-zero cost weights since splitting the large create() (2379B) and main (1674B) bodies multiplies structure for downstream passes at negligible runtime impact. ICALL and IGV are emphasized for diversity — indirect calls disrupt static call-graph recovery of the templated node_t::intersect pair, and inter-group variable shuffling hinders data-flow correlation across split blocks. BCF and IBR are raised moderately but their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights remain the highest among cheap passes because this is a compute-bound ray-tracing benchmark with a recursive create() on the hot path, so opaque-predicate and branch overhead must stay bounded. FLA is the most restrained pass: flattening the two intersect instantiations plus create() would inflate a 6.5KB text section substantially and add dispatcher overhead on the FP-hot inner loop, so its cost weights keep it selective rather than program-wide. CorrectnessRisk weights stay low everywhere since round 0 showed clean codegen, but FLA retains the highest risk weight as FP-heavy flattened loops are the most correctness-sensitive transform in this profile.
